posts.title: Not a studio. A lab.
posts.copy:
A studio executes the idea you already have.
A lab goes looking for the one nobody has tried yet.

We're Sensa Lab. We build interactive experiences for brands: AI mirrors, arcade-style games, sensor-driven installations, things people walk up to and actually touch.

New website is live. Take a look at what we've been building → sensalab.io
posts.note: Relanzamiento. Story 1: arte 'a Lab'. Story 2: 'Visit our website' con link sticker.

posts.title: Based in LA. Global by design.
posts.copy:
Home base: Los Angeles.
Team and partners: Mexico City, Miami and wherever the project lands.

Our last AI commercial was built by a crew in Russia for a brand launching in Brazil. That's pretty normal for us. Time zones are a scheduling problem, not a creative one.

If you're an agency or brand with an activation coming up, we'd like to hear about it.

posts.title: Not all interactive experiences share the same goal
posts.copy:
Before picking the tech, pick the job.

The Simulator lets people try the product before they buy it.
The Collector trades a fun moment for real lead data.
The Advocate turns guests into the ones posting about your brand.

Same screen, same sensors, totally different build depending on the KPI. Which one is your next event?

posts.title: Avatars that perform
posts.copy:
Digital avatars that talk back, react to the crowd and stay in character for an eight-hour show day.

We build the real-time pipeline behind them: motion capture, voice, rendering and the logic that keeps it from breaking when 300 people show up at once.

posts.title: Top AI experiential booths
posts.copy:
Three AI booths we keep coming back to:

Intel at CES made data processing something you could see happen in front of you.
Salesforce at Dreamforce turned attendee data into AI trading cards people actually kept.
Vonage told its cloud story through an interactive hero you got to play.

The common thread: none of them explained the product. They let you use it. Swipe for the breakdown.

posts.title: Perception vs. Reality
posts.copy:
What people think: interactive tech is fragile and something will crash in front of the client.

What actually happens when it's built right: it runs all day, the queue keeps growing and nobody thinks about the tech at all.

Most of our work is the boring part nobody sees. Testing, backups, a plan B for the Wi-Fi.

posts.title: What is white label?
posts.copy:
For agencies: you sell the experience, we build it.

We work white label with experiential agencies in the US and Mexico. Development, real-time logic, hardware and on-site tech, all under your brand. Your client never has to know we exist (unless you want to brag about us).

DMs are open.

posts.title: Why traditional marketing isn't working anymore
posts.copy:
Walk any expo floor and count the booths with a banner, a looping video and someone handing out pens.

Now count the ones with a line.

People don't remember what a brand told them. They remember what they did there. That's the whole case for experiential.

posts.title: The brands you remember don't just advertise
posts.copy:
Nike x SNIPES in Brooklyn: a photo booth that turned every visitor into a content creator.
Adidas 'Faster Than': treadmills in-store, real-time metrics, the product proving itself.
Adidas in Dubai: a billboard you could literally swim in.

None of these were about budget. They were about giving people something to do. Which one would you have stood in line for?

posts.title: Get the playbook
posts.copy:
Turn attendees into players.

A touch game, a leaderboard or a sensor floor gives people a reason to stay at your booth longer, and every round is a lead you can follow up with.

We've packaged our favorite game mechanics into ready-to-brand experiences. Ask us for the playbook.

posts.copy:
Same square footage, same budget, very different result.

Swipe to see the small changes that take a booth from 'walk past' to 'wait, what is that?'

posts.title: Is your activation just for decoration?
posts.copy:
If it looks great in photos but nobody touches it, it's decoration.

An activation should do a job: capture leads, explain the product, get people posting. If you can't name the job, the build isn't done yet.
